# railway_deployment (Data Source)

The latest deployment of a service in an environment. Terraform reads it when it plans, so it reports the deployment as of the plan; set `wait_for_deployment` on `railway_service` to have an apply wait for its deployment instead.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "railway_service" "web" {
  environment_id = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"
  name           = "web"
  source         = { image = { image = "traefik/whoami:v1.10" } }

  # Fail the apply if the deployment it starts does not succeed.
  wait_for_deployment = { timeout = "15m" }
}

data "railway_deployment" "web" {
  environment_id = railway_service.web.environment_id
  service_id     = railway_service.web.railway_id
}

output "web_status" {
  value = data.railway_deployment.web.status
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `environment_id` (String) Environment ID.
- `service_id` (String) Railway service ID, such as `railway_service.web.railway_id`.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) When Railway created the deployment.
- `id` (String) Deployment ID.
- `static_url` (String) Railway domain the deployment serves, when it has one.
- `status` (String) Deployment status, such as `SUCCESS`, `BUILDING`, `DEPLOYING`, `FAILED` or `CRASHED`.
- `updated_at` (String) When the deployment last changed.
- `url` (String) URL of the deployment, when it has one.
